context:
Treat trend rendering as a data-contract issue first and an SVG issue second.
Decide the duplicate-day semantics, then make TimeSeries consume point-level
identity data and render only claims the read model can support.
description:
Platform detail trend charts can render multiple observations for the same
platform and date while every point title repeats the identity of the first
run in the series. On `/results/p/duckdb/`, the chart showed three points
whose titles all referenced the same DuckDB result even though they came from
different rows.

This is not just a tooltip bug. The current time-series contract groups by
platform ID and uses `run_date` as the x-axis, but the read model can contain
multiple same-day submissions with different result IDs and no time-of-day
ordering. The UI must decide how to represent duplicate-day observations
before drawing lines that imply a chronology that the data may not provide.

anti_patterns.dont: aggregate duplicate runs without naming the aggregation policy.
fix repeated titles by appending array indexes with no user-visible meaning.
jitter duplicate dates unless the jitter corresponds to a real timestamp or documented sequence.
suppress trend charts without giving users a path to the underlying runs.

preserves.behavior: Point titles and aria text must identify the actual point/result being inspected.
Sparse or duplicate-day states must still let users inspect underlying result rows.
The fix must not drop valid historical data silently.
Trend charts must not imply a chronological ordering that is not present in the data.

results-explorer/src/components/TimeSeries.tsx groups by platform ID and currently builds series labels from the first entry.

work_units.notes:
Decide how the UI treats multiple runs for the same platform/cohort/date
before changing the chart. Acceptable outcomes include:
  - hide the line chart for duplicate-day series and show a compact
    duplicate-run table;
  - aggregate duplicate-day points by a named policy such as latest
    published run, best valid run, or median, while exposing the run count;
  - render duplicate-day points as distinct observations only if the read
    model includes a real timestamp or deterministic sequence field.
Decision gate: do not jitter points or connect duplicate-day runs with a
line unless the policy explains the implied ordering and tie handling.
work_units.summary: Choose and document duplicate-day trend semantics

work_units.notes:
Update `TimeSeries` so each point title and accessible label is built from
that point's result identity, date, and metric value, not from the first
entry in the series. If the component only receives series-level metadata,
extend the narrow chart entry shape to carry the minimum fields needed for
point-level identity under the public run-identity contract.
work_units.summary: Make trend point titles and accessibility text point-specific

work_units.notes:
Apply the duplicate-day policy consistently on platform detail and any chart
panel using `TimeSeries`. If aggregation is chosen, show the aggregation
policy and duplicate count. If chart suppression is chosen, show a compact
state that explains why a trend line is unavailable and gives access to the
underlying runs. If distinct points are chosen, use a data-backed sequence
field rather than layout-only jitter.
work_units.summary: Implement the chosen duplicate-day display policy
